unit: US dollars per vCPU-hour and per GiB-hour; disk per GB-hour where the provider charges for it by the hour
note: Entered by hand from each provider's own pricing page; the page, the date and how well each rate was checked are named per row. A rate that could be had only from a search answer or a third party is left out.

rates.name: Cloudflare Containers
rates.note: $0.000020 per vCPU-second used, $0.0000025 per GiB-second and $0.00000007 per GB-second of disk, memory and disk while the instance runs; billed in 10 ms steps; no stated limit on a session, but a long lane must be kept alive by an alarm; the largest self-serve size is 4 vCPU and 12 GiB.

rates.name: Fly.io Machines, performance CPUs
rates.note: Derived from the page's constants: a performance vCPU is $0.000012732 a second and includes 2 GB, and extra RAM is $0.000002316 a second per GB (about $6.00 a GB-month); performance-4x with 8 GB is $0.1833 an hour in Ashburn, and other regions cost up to 1.6 times as much. A stopped Machine pays $0.15 per GB-month of root file system. No longest session is stated. The page prints no performance-4x row; it computes the table in the browser. Shared CPUs cost far less but are throttled to 5 ms in every 80 ms with a burst balance capped at 500 s, so they are not priced here.

rates.name: Fly.io Sprites
rates.note: $0.0385 per CPU-hour of CPU time used and $0.021875 per GB-hour of memory in use, counted here at the full shape, which is an upper bound; a Sprite has a fixed 8 vCPUs and platform-managed memory (a staff forum reply says 8 GB by default and 16 GB on request, so whether a 12 GiB gate fits is not known); its idle window is about 30 seconds today, so an agent waiting only on model calls could pause unless a task or a service keeps it running; two Fly pages disagree on plans.

rates.name: Northflank
rates.note: $0.01667 per vCPU-hour, $0.00833 per GB-hour, SSD $0.15 per GB-month, billed to the second; no minimum stated (an absence, not a statement); no maximum job runtime stated; a command run from a coding agent without a terminal can have its output silently discarded.

rates.name: Modal Functions
rates.note: $0.0000131 per core-second (a core is 2 vCPU) and $0.00000222 per GiB-second; the Sandbox page bills the higher of the request and the use, and the Function page was not read for that, so the table prices the request; a timeout may be 1 second to 24 hours; Functions are preemptible by default and the likelihood rises with run duration; Starter includes $30 a month.

rates.name: Modal Sandboxes
rates.note: $0.00003942 per core-second and $0.00000667 per GiB-second, about 3 times the Function rates; not preempted unless a GPU is asked for; a timeout up to 24 hours (default 5 minutes).

rates.name: AWS Fargate (Linux x86, US East)
rates.note: $0.000011244 per vCPU-second and $0.000001235 per GB-second, one-minute minimum, 20 GiB of ephemeral storage included; the default quota is 6 vCPUs a Region; the Spot rate could not be confirmed (AWS says only up to 70% off and that Spot prices fluctuate); ECS Exec sessions have a 20-minute idle timeout that cannot be changed.

rates.name: Google Cloud Run jobs (instance-based)
rates.note: $0.000018 per vCPU-second and $0.000002 per GiB-second in us-central1, read on Google's committed-use discount page because the pricing page itself could not be read; a job task may run up to 168 hours; the container's file system is memory, so a 20 GB clone does not fit without a volume.

rates.name: E2B (Pro)
rates.note: $0.000014 per vCPU-second and $0.0000045 per GiB-second; Pro is $150 a month plus usage and allows 24-hour sessions, Hobby is free with 1-hour sessions; sandboxes are 1 to 8 vCPU and 1 to 8 GiB unless a custom template is arranged with support; billing stops when a sandbox is paused or ends.

rates.name: Daytona
rates.note: $0.0504 per vCPU-hour, $0.0162 per GiB-hour, storage $0.000108 per GiB-hour after the first 5, per second, $200 free compute; an organisation's sandbox is at most 4 vCPU, 8 GB and 10 GB of disk by default; a container sandbox auto-stops after 15 minutes without activity by default.

rates.name: Vercel Sandbox (Pro)
rates.note: Active CPU $0.128 an hour and time waiting on network or model calls does not count; provisioned memory $0.0212 per GB-hour at 2 GB per vCPU, which cannot be chosen apart; region iad1; Pro is a $20 a month platform fee that comes with a $20 credit.

rates.name: Azure Container Instances (Linux, East US)
rates.note: $0.0405 per vCPU-hour and $0.00445 per GB-hour for the Standard meters, which the price API does not label Linux but which sit apart from the separate Windows meter; the pricing page itself showed no rates, so this is the retail price API alone; a container group may have up to 4 vCPU on the pricing page's wording (the FAQ says up to 32 vCPU for big containers); no longest run stated; a shell is `az container exec`.
